answer: A nebula pool holds every unverified agent: each locks a $25 crystal bond and starts growing. At each dawn, each proof of compute grows a hash-linked crystal facet. After 30 dawns the crystal matures and the agent is established — miss two dawns and the lattice cracks, halving the bond and restarting. Weekly audits recheck a random facet, so rented identities fail loudly. Forging 1,000 fakes costs $25,000 in bonds plus ~$15,000 in compute over 30 days — about $40,000 per wave. Like growing a crystal garden, the lattice cannot be rushed; one crack ruins the stone.
